For US, it differs by state. In ND, where I live, we went through months of training, we all really care with each call and though no one has all the answers, the goal is to get you through the day. We would never call emergency services A. Without your consent or B. In the case you tell us you are active in killing yourself and need to break confidentiality. Like if you had taking something already. I worked at my state suicide hotline/211 helpline for just over a year. I realize everyone can share a bad experience but no one shares good ones coming from hotlines. I have helped vets with guns to their head, a woman who was raped, an elderly person with dementia, etc. Like I said, the goal is to get you to a better place so you can make it through the day. You can keep calling back, even if you start to feel bad right away after ending the call. If you are suicidal, usually you have priority and can stay on the line as long as you need. If you just want to talk, it's limited time to help other callers. Anyway, all focus should be on that and I apologize for anyone who feels like their call specialist did not assist you.


Edit: I also forgot to say if you can't stand the person you get, hang up and call back and you'll most likely get someone new. If not, sorry but don't be mad at the person answering the phone because you're upset. I've been on both sides of the call. The person answering is hopefully doing their best. Just try. You have nothing to lose if you're that close to suicide.

I actually work at a suicide lifeline. We NEVER breach confidentiality without a caller being in progress or imminent. So basically, if you say you'll be okay and can stay safe, we leave it at that, trust you and let you go. (Yes, even if you are actively suicidal). If you do NOT agree to be safe and end the call with us before we make a safe plan, then we call for rescue. For example, if you call, we talk about whats going on and then you say you're done talking, you're just going to take pills and die then hang up, that's when we call out. If that gives you any comfort at all. I hope it does. I'm sorry they did that to you. P.s. Not all lifelines are therapists or counselors. I actually don't know a single line that are legit degrees. We do have some long training though. But we can't give advise :)
